S-01 Level capacity update (OrderSuccess queue)

Bangla name: লেভেল ধারণক্ষমতা হালনাগাদ (OrderSuccess কিউ)

← 50 · System-initiated · Contents · Open queries

1. Name and purpose

Level capacity update. A seat level (one gallery, block and level of an event) has a capacity in the database and a live capacity in Redis. When a paid order or an admin action changes the number of seats, the change is put on the OrderSuccess queue; the Booking worker LevelCapacityUpdateService reads it, writes the new capacity to the database, and finishes the Redis bookkeeping. Concepts: queue-driven processing, Redis live capacity, background workers, distributed locks.

2. Trigger and actor

  • Producer (user order): Booking, when a payment is confirmed: DgePay callback HandleDgePayment, the re-check job RevaildateRecentPendingBookingsAsync (S-05), and the handler behind the anonymous GET payment-status-bypass, which marks the order Paid without asking the gateway (HandleDgePaymentBypass, see X-18). The SSLCommerz handler publishes the same message but is inactive (Appendix A).
  • Producer (admin): CapacityManager.BookLevelCapacity for admin capacity adjustments and seat reservations (A-10, A-11).
  • Consumer: Booking service, LevelCapacityUpdateService (no user; no token).

3. Business flow

A customer reserves seats; the seats are held in a short "locked" list for 12 minutes while they pay. When the payment succeeds, the seats are permanently removed from the level's availability. If the customer is an admin (complimentary or partner tickets), the live count is changed at once and the database follows through the queue.

4. Technical flow

  1. Hold at order creation [HTTP + user token] UserBookingOrderManager.CreateAsync takes the locks user_booking:{userId} and level_booking_{event}_{gallery}_{block}_{level} (X-25) and calls CapacityManager.BookLevelCapacity. For a user order this only writes the order to the Redis hash level_locked:{event}_{gallery}_{block}_{level} (field = order id); expired entries (older than 12 minutes) are removed first, and the call fails with no_seats_available, order_limit_exceeded or seat_limit_exceeded when the numbers do not fit.
  2. Publish on success [SQS: OrderSuccess] with a LevelCapacityUpdate message: orderType, amount, hasSeats, seats, isIncrease, groupId ({event}_{gallery}_{block}_{level}), orderId, capacityAction (Booking, Allocation or Reservation). For user orders the message is sent only if the payment is Paid (DgePay callback: only when the order is no more than 12 minutes old).
  3. For an admin action BookLevelCapacity changes the Redis hash capacity field level_live:{...} directly (atomic increment/decrement, no lock needed), updates the live seat string, then publishes the same message so the database catches up.
  4. Worker [Worker: 1 min start delay, then every 30 s; RedLock level_capacity_updater_{0..49}, expiry 30 s, wait 10 s]: LevelCapacityUpdateService takes one random slot lock and runs LevelCapacityUpdateTaskManager once. The task manager long-reads the queue (MaxNumberOfMessages 5, WaitTimeSeconds 0, visibility 60 s) and, per message: - CapacityManager.UpdateLevelCapacityAsync takes the lock database_update_{event}_{gallery}_{block}_{level} (expiry 5 s, wait 30 s), adds or subtracts amount on TicketingCapacity in the database (error if it would go below 0), and adjusts the stored seat lists when hasSeats; - for orderType = User: HashDecrement capacity level_live:{groupId} by amount, HashDelete level_locked:{groupId} for the order id, and, with seats, remove the seats from the live seat string; - the message is deleted only after success. On an exception the message is not deleted; it becomes visible again after 60 s.
  5. In parallel, BookLevelCapacity also publishes an EventCapacity message (S-02).

5. Components

Kind Component
Services Booking (API, worker); consumer and producer are the same service
Queue OrderSuccess (AWS:Queue:OrderSuccess)
Tables Capacities rows of the Booking schema (TicketingCapacity, Seats, LockedSeats), UserBookingOrder
Redis capacity hash (level_live:*, level_live_seats:*), level_locked:* hashes, refresh set, locks
Code Services/Booking/ETP.Booking.Service/Workers/BackgroundServices/LevelCapacityUpdateService.cs, .../TaskManagers/LevelCapacityUpdateTaskManager.cs, Services/Booking/ETP.Booking.Domain/Managers/CapacityManager.cs
Config AWS:Queue:OrderSuccess, Cache:Redis:*, DistributedLock:Redis:* (X-26)

6. API contracts

No endpoint of its own. The queue message (Core/ETP.Core/Queue/Messages/LevelCapacityUpdate.cs), serialised with System.Text.Json defaults (PascalCase property names, enums as numbers):

{
  "OrderType": 0,
  "Amount": 2,
  "HasSeats": false,
  "Seats": null,
  "IsIncrease": false,
  "GroupId": "101_5_12_33",
  "OrderId": "<order public id>",
  "CapacityAction": 0
}

(illustrative values; OrderType and CapacityAction are enum numbers whose names come from Enums.OrderType and CapacityAction). The queue is a FIFO queue only when its configured name ends with fifo; then GroupId is the MessageGroupId (so one level is processed in order) and OrderId is the de-duplication id (SqsPublisher).

7. Data and side effects

  • Database: TicketingCapacity (and seat columns) of one level row.
  • Redis: live capacity decremented, locked order removed, live seats trimmed.
  • Failure handling: failed messages are retried after the visibility timeout; there is no dead-letter handling in code [UNCONFIRMED: Q-09].

9. Handover notes

  1. Throughput is bounded by the polling design. Each instance runs one 5-message batch (no long polling), then sleeps 30 s. At most 10 messages per minute per instance, so a burst of paid orders reaches the database with a delay (derived from the constants above; observe in your environment).
  2. Two sources of truth for a level. Between the Redis decrement and the database update the two disagree; the lock-and-queue design accepts that. A Redis flush loses the live counters (X-25).
  3. The 12-minute rule appears in three places (callback age check, BookLevelCapacity, the refresh worker). A DgePay callback that arrives after 12 minutes neither changes the order status nor publishes OrderSuccess; the comment in code says such an order "is cancelled by BG service" (S-05).
  4. Key mismatch in the bypass handler. On Failed, HandleDgePaymentBypass deletes the field from level_locked_{EventId}_... (underscore, public event id) while the rest of the code uses level_locked:{EventLongId}_...; the entry is therefore not removed there and lapses by the 12-minute rule [UNCONFIRMED: Q-10].
  5. No dead-letter queue is visible in code; a poison message is retried forever each minute. Queue configuration (redrive policy) is in AWS, not in the repository.
  6. If the message body cannot be deserialised (null), the task manager skips it with continue and does not delete it, so it also returns to the queue.

Depends on: order creation (P-06), published event and levels (A-07). Affects: seat availability shown to every customer (P-04), S-02, S-04, the capacity reports.
